# api-sync-report — core-ledger

**Verdict:** FAIL
**Run at:** 2026-10-20 (run 1, mode: first run)
**Generated by:** `api-forge` (sdlc plugin) protocol step 8 (inline drift check)
**Sources read:** PRD.md ✓ · data-model.md ✓ · sad.md §5/§6/§8/§11/§12 ✓ · adr/0001–0006 ✓ · CONTEXT.md ✓ (via sad.md §12) · `.size` ✓ (M → full surface)
**Scenario:** A — `data-model.md` exists, so every field traces to a typed column and `unresolved_origins` is empty.
**Contract version:** `info.version: 0.1.0`, OpenAPI 3.1.0
**Rules file:** `.claude/rules/openapi.md` **bootstrapped** on this run (was absent) — baseline + a `## FinNavis deviations` section. You own that file from now on.
**Surface:** `backend-service` — read from `sad.md` frontmatter `target_surfaces`, not re-derived.

## Why FAIL

Core points 1–3 all hold. The verdict is FAIL for one reason, and it is a deliberate choice, not a
broken derivation:

> **`category_groups` is a table in `data-model.md` with no operation that creates one.**
> AC-11 ("creates a category, **with or without a group**") and AC-13 ("moves it to **another
> group**") both need a group id that nothing in this API can produce. You chose
> **Fix-the-source-first** over inventing endpoints with no user story behind them, which by the
> skill's verdict rules is a `FAIL`.

The contract **was still written** — 15 operations covering everything that is derivable today, so
it is reviewable now and `--reconcile` only has to add the missing surface. It is marked not-final
in its header comment. **No handoff to `break-tasks`.**

**No `PRD §5 ↔ data-model` contradiction found**, so the "take the stricter value" rule did not fire.

One alignment worth naming: `amount > 0` (AC-02) is **not** expressed as a schema constraint. A
regex cannot cleanly reject `0.0000`, and `data-model.md` decision 6 puts the rule in the Domain
entity rather than a `CHECK`. The contract therefore documents it on `MoneyAmount` and returns
`*.amount_not_positive`. The constraint and the contract agree about *where* the rule lives.

**The reverse direction fails on one entity.**

> **`category_groups` — `# unused-in-prd`, and worse than unused.**
> The table exists in `data-model.md` with `id`, `name` UNIQUE and `created_at`. No PRD §4 user
> story creates, lists, renames or deletes a group, and `sad.md` §5 declares no use case for it
> either — `Application/Categories/` holds only `Create, Rename, MoveToGroup, Delete`.
>
> This is not a harmless orphan table. **AC-11 and AC-13 are both half-unreachable through this
> API**: a client can create a category without a group and move one out of a group, but there is
> no way to obtain a `category_group_id` to pass in the other direction. The feature's own §2 goal
> — "answers both group totals and category totals" — depends on groups existing.
>
> **Resolved as: Fix-the-source-first.** No group endpoints were invented.

> **`Categories/Rename` — `# orphan-sequence`.**
> `sad.md` §5 declares the use case and the `Presentation/Endpoints/Categories/Rename/` folder, but
> no §4 user story and no §5 acceptance criterion covers renaming a category. US-04 lists "create
> categories, optionally put them in a group, and move them between groups" — rename is absent.
> (AC-08 covers renaming an *account*, not a category.)
>
> **Resolved as: Fix-the-source-first.** No `renameCategory` operation was generated. Either add the
> story to the PRD, or drop the folder from `sad.md` §5 — the two artifacts currently disagree.

Two smaller coverage notes, not resolved as findings:

- **No "list categories" operation.** AC-11 says a new category "becomes available to name when
  recording a transaction", but no AC asks to read the list back and `sad.md` §5 declares no use
  case. Not invented. Worth adding to the PRD alongside the group stories — a client cannot build a
  category picker without it.
- **No plain "list accounts" operation.** `getAccountBalances` returns every account with its name
  and balance, which satisfies AC-07's "appears in the account list". Accept-as-is.

- **No `Idempotency-Key` on any mutating endpoint, and no `contracts/events.md`** —
  `sad.md` §6 states it outright: *"No flow in this feature is asynchronous. Every one is request
  and response, so none carries an idempotency key, a retry note or a dead-letter branch."*

  which is what AC-07's "appears in the account list" needs.
- **Money crosses the wire as a `string`** — deviation 2 in `.claude/rules/openapi.md`. A JSON number
  is an IEEE double in most clients and loses the fourth decimal place of `NUMERIC(19,4)`.

## Decisions settled at this gate

Three open items were explicitly handed to `/sdlc-api-forge` by the upstream artifacts. All three are
now closed:

1. **History page size.** `sad.md` §6 ("History paging is drawn but never specified… `/sdlc-api-forge`
   needs a page size, and PRD §8 has no open question covering it") and `data-model.md` Open items.
   → **`limit`: minimum 1, maximum 200, default 50.** PRD §6 budgets p95 ≤ 400 ms per page over
   ~20 000 movements; at ~550 movements a month the default pulls a month in about eleven requests.

2. **Does a category filter on history exclude transfers?** `sad.md` §6 ("AC-16 pulls in two
   directions here… The PRD does not say this, so confirm it at `/sdlc-api-forge`").
   → **Yes.** A transfer carries no `category_id`, so it can never match the filter; returning it
   anyway would mean the result did not all match what was asked. Documented on the `category_id`
   query parameter of `getHistory`.

3. **Paging style for the `UNION ALL` history.** `sad.md` §11 ("Decided at `/sdlc-api-forge`, which
   owns the endpoint contract… a merged keyset page over date and id is workable").
   → **Cursor, keyset over `(occurred_on, id)`**, matching the api-forge default of cursor over
   offset. `id` is a time-ordered UUID v7 (ADR-0005), which `data-model.md` already names as "a
   tiebreaker when paging history by date". The cursor is an opaque string rather than a bare UUID,
   because one id cannot locate a boundary across two tables — deviation 3 in
   `.claude/rules/openapi.md`.
